title: Introduce cost-fabricator: rules engine + quant telemetry adapter
author: Priya Malhotra
release_notes: Adds a tenant-level cost rules engine (cost-fabricator) and a quantization telemetry adapter. Enables per-tenant policy enforcement for batching, cache fallbacks, and quant profile selection. No breaking API changes. Backwards-compatible defaults included.
body:
Context and motivation: We need a lightweight runtime-side rules engine to apply tenant cost policies (budget caps, preferred quant tiers, cache retention hints) close to the routing layer. Existing heuristics are scattered across scheduler/optimizer and CLI tooling, making rollout and observability slow. This PR introduces 'cost-fabricator', a small deterministic rules engine plus a 'quant-telemetry-adapter' that surfaces quantization efficacy signals (token-savings vs. quality delta) into the rules evaluation path so routing and fallback decisions can be made with direct telemetry.

What this PR does (high level): - New cost-fabricator service module (runtime/rules): evaluation DAG, templated policy language, safe-evaluation sandbox. - Quant telemetry adapter (telemetry/quant_adapter): aggregates per-model quant metrics (accuracy delta, token savings, failed-degradation-rate) and exposes a compact score. - Router integration: routing/policy layer can now call cost-fabricator.evaluate(tenant_id, workload_signature) synchronously (<=2ms p50) to get action suggestions: prefer_batch_profile, cache_ttl_hint, quant_tier_hint, fallback_model_set. - Defaults: introduces conservative tenant defaults and a tenant-overrides table stored in config store. - Tests: unit + integration harness that runs synthetic tenant policies against the routing simulator.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-2031) - [x] Rules engine core + evaluator - [x] Quant telemetry adapter + ingestion path - [x] Router integration + small synchronous API - [x] Unit tests and integration tests in sim harness - [x] Telemetry metrics and dashboard panels (ops) - [x] Backwards compatible defaults and migration notes

Commits (summary): - c1: initial rules-engine scaffolding and evaluation DSL - c2: add policy templates and tenant override plumbing - c3: quant telemetry adapter and ingestion consumer - c4: router integration and synchronous evaluation API - c5: tests + sim harness updates - c6: metrics, dashboards, and docs updates

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/rules/engine.py (new) - runtime/rules/dsl.md (new) - runtime/rules/tenants.py (new) - telemetry/quant_adapter/consumer.py (new) - telemetry/quant_adapter/score.py (new) - router/policy_integration.py (modified) - config/tenant_defaults.yaml (modified) - sim/smoke/policy_sim.py (modified) - tests/unit/test_rules_engine.py (new) - tests/integration/test_router_evaluate.py (new) - docs/ops/cost_fabricator.md (new) - dashboards/cost_fabricator.jsonnet (new) - infra/helm/values-cost-fabricator.yaml (new) - ci/pipeline/cost-fabricator-tests.yml (new)

Patch highlights and rationale: - Evaluation DSL: intentionally small (only logical operators, numeric threshold, and simple time-window aggregation) to keep evaluation deterministic and auditable. We avoid Turing-complete constructs to make rollout safe. - Quant score: a single float in [-1,1] where negative indicates quality regressions outweigh savings; positive favors more aggressive quant tiers. The score logic is pluggable for future ML-derived heuristics. - Synchronous API: kept sub-2ms by caching compiled policies and pre-warming tenant overrides in memory; we added metrics to monitor tail latency.

Review conversation (abridged, chronological): - Diego Alvarez (2026-02-17): "Nice direction. Can you add e2e test for a tenant with a tight budget that forces fallback to smaller batch sizes? Also please call out expected memory impact of keeping compiled policies in-process." - Priya Malhotra (2026-02-18): "Added sim test and documented memory footprint (~1.2MB per tenant policy compiled). Will add monitoring alert to catch growth." - Marta Nguyen (2026-02-20): "Lgtm but unit tests flaked in CI on windows runner, looks like path normalization in the sim harness. Please make path handling OS-agnostic." - Priya Malhotra (2026-02-21): "Fixed path normalization and re-ran tests. Added a small fixture to simulate Windows-style paths." - Liam O'Connor (2026-02-24): "A few nit: rename 'prefer_batch_profile' -> 'batch_profile_hint' for clarity; also add an integration test where quant adapter reports a transient spike in degradation and ensure router respects fallback policy." - Priya Malhotra (2026-02-25): "Renamed field and added integration test. Also implemented exponential backoff in fallback decisions to avoid oscillation." - CI run (2026-02-26): first run failed (flake in tests/integration/test_router_evaluate.py due to timing). Re-ran; second run passed (2026-02-27).

CI summary: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests: pass (after fix) - Lint: pass - Typecheck: pass - Benchmark: small regressions noted in canary runs (p99 latency +0.6ms) — accepted after perf review because decision path remains within SLO and optimizations scheduled (ENG-2109).

Performance and safety considerations: - We added a new low-timeout synchronous path; measured medians are ~0.9ms, p95 under 2.5ms. We introduced a configurable circuit-breaker: if cost-fabricator latency exceeds 10ms or error rate >1%, router falls back to safe default policy. - Default conservative rules ensure no tenant suddenly opts into aggressive quant without explicit override and telemetry-confirmation. - We limit the size of compiled policies and enforce a max-clauses guard to prevent runaway policies.

Deployment plan: - stage: deploy to staging small cluster with feature flag 'cost_fabricator:v1' enabled for 5 canary tenants - monitor metrics/dashboards for latency and unit economics delta - after 48h and manual sign-off, enable for more tenants with progressive ramp - add rollout notes to release docs

Post-merge follow-ups (tracked in ENG-2109): - Add a feedback loop to promote quant tiers automatically after N successful requests - Explore ML-based scoring for quant_adapter (keeps pluggable) - Tighten bench perf: inline simple policies and reduce p99 by ~0.4ms

Notes for reviewers: The rules DSL intentionally keeps expressivity low for auditability. The quant adapter aggregates model-reported metrics and is deliberately conservative when producing positive scores. If we want to expand rules, we should add authorizations and review gates.
